CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine follow-up with chronic medical conditions and fatigue.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
61-year-old male presents for routine follow-up. Patient reports increased fatigue, which he attributes to age and feeling drained at the end of the day. He continues to ride his road bike 20-30 miles at a time, though notes he cannot maintain the speed he previously could and tires easily after long rides. He used to complete 40-mile rides and could outpace his friend Tyler, but now feels fatigued and requires rest upon arriving home. Patient is concerned about his aortic valve replacement, which was performed on 1/22/2013. He notes he is approximately 8 years out from surgery and recalls being told the valve would last about 8 years. His last stress test was on 9/9/2019. He requested an echocardiogram to assess current valve function. He denies significant changes since last visit. Patient no longer follows up at Hopkins due to stress. Patient reports his wife and other physicians have noted he pursues his lips when breathing, but he denies associated wheezing and is able to maintain his cycling activities. Patient also reports a small nodule on his right epididymis that he noticed but is not particularly concerned about. Denies that fatigue is related to depression; describes himself as a happy person overall. Sleep varies from 6-7 hours nightly. Works in a lecture capacity, attempting morning workouts and swimming twice weekly at 5:45 AM. Wife reports he snores slightly but has never mentioned him stopping breathing.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies wheezing. Denies depression. Denies changes in breathing associated with exertion beyond expected fatigue. No mention of night sweats, weight changes, or other constitutional symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair on 1/22/2013.
Hyperlipidemia (based on prior lipid panel).

MEDICATIONS
Vitamin D3: 50,000 units on Sundays, 2,000 units on the other six days of the week.
Clindamycin prior to dental procedures.

ALLERGIES
Not documented in this visit.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented in this visit.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as a lecturer. Exercises regularly, cycling 20-30 miles at a time on a road bike. Swims twice weekly at 5:45 AM. Denies routine testicular self-exams. Married. Snores mildly per spouse report. COVID-19 vaccination completed with first dose on 1/15/2021 and second dose on 2/5/2021. Does not follow up at Hopkins.

General: Overall well-appearing male.
Respiratory: Pursed lip breathing noted with low exhalation phase. Clear to auscultation, no wheezing.
Genitalia: Right testicle with 2-3 millimeter palpable nodule on epididymis. Left testicle normal. No hernia palpable.
All other portions of physical exam: Normal.

- Alkaline phosphatase: 156 (elevated)
- Total cholesterol: 247
- HDL: 66
- LDL: 166

- TSH: 2.68 (normal)
- CBC: Unremarkable

New labs ordered pending results.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

History of aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair: Patient is 8 years post-op from surgery on 1/22/2013, asymptomatic, and doing well overall. He is not currently followed by cardiology. Plan: Referral to cardiology (Dr. Vincent Sanchez recommended). Echocardiogram and stress test ordered for further evaluation. Follow-up in 1 year or sooner if needed.

Elevated alkaline phosphatase: Most recent labs showed elevation at 156. Likely related to bone health, though liver pathology cannot be excluded. Plan: Repeat alkaline phosphatase and GGT labs ordered today. Results will be reviewed and communicated via patient portal unless significantly abnormal, in which case patient will be called.

Pursed lip breathing with low exhalation phase: Patient noted to have this finding on exam and reports increased fatigue with exertion despite maintaining 20-30 mile cycling distances. No associated wheezing. Plan: Pulmonary function tests ordered for further evaluation.

Right testicular nodule: 2-3 millimeter palpable nodule noted on right epididymis on exam. No hernia. Plan: Referral to urology for possible ultrasound.

Preventive health: Most recent labs otherwise unremarkable. COVID-19 vaccination complete. Plan: MMR vaccine to be administered today. Shingles vaccine recommended; front desk to schedule for next month.

Patient counseled on plan and agrees. To return in 1 year for wellness visit, sooner if needed. Instructed to call with any questions or concerns.
